approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from the current session's scored archive, using crossover and mutation to build fresh pools. It fits the original count-fingerprint Gaussian process for location, candidate eligibility and correlated latent draws. A fixed native quantile model sees all count coordinates through the measured full-coordinate adapter: variable columns keep their fitted transformations and training-constant columns remain visible as centered query counts. Its eight fitted views supply a bounded, piecewise-linear conditional quantile law. The Parent centers that law at the Gaussian-process mean and chooses sequential sampled maxima, retaining its stall mask, stable ties and real-feedback update loop.
approach.novelty: Combine that completed input adapter with the donor's variance-preserving Gaussian residual projection. The adapted native law supplies exactly the same variance, but each residual becomes a scaled copy of the existing standardized Gaussian draw; bounded tails, asymmetry and higher moments change jointly. The earlier Gaussianization experiment used filtered inputs and improved productive offspring gain while losing endpoint score. There are no completed same-Parent siblings in this brief. This experiment tests that operation on the adapted nonzero-query input, with a new requirement that both full and late productive gain improve. It preserves the separate endpoint goal and does not assume the two earlier gains add.

observed_bottleneck: The actual code Parent n-ada68e100737 executes its full-coordinate residual adapter throughout the complete Search panel, yet its productive gain weakens late and does not reach the endpoint goal. Its three summary.json and run.log files report all fifteen cells ok, 4350 optimizer purchases, zero invalid/duplicate attempts, mean final Top-1 0.5622564516615843 and seed population SD 0.005481732549278124. The paired mean against its own code Parent n-e2506e11f536 is +0.0032675763122120096, with seed deltas +0.0065564998425270415, -0.02371722376057095 and +0.026963452854679937. All 435 native allocations and 420 probes execute; full positive gain over actual generating parents is 16.68612674725103, but late gain is 3.915646383849673, down from 4.445967758637079 on its own Parent. Against formal Anchor n-cf8d309c06de, its endpoint mean is -0.04477386454954668. The donor n-a03f82e62383 implements the exact direct centered-variance Gaussianization helper and raises full/late gain on filtered inputs to 15.095384787005024/5.38387288825771, while its endpoint falls -0.01919444902573131 against n-e2506e11f536. This supports a specific input-by-shape transfer test, not a claim of endpoint benefit. The plan audit at policy/scratch/r0065-00-improve-L01/plan-evidence-audit.json recomputes the Parent gain from the existing Analyze paid-row extraction and independently joins all 4350 rows and their chronological generating-parent scores to published trajectories; it is not a new full-log numerical reconstruction. The frozen catalog leaves this interaction unresolved and preserves the donor endpoint counterexample.

hypothesis: On the actual Parent full-coordinate native quantile law Q^A_i, retain m^A_i = integral_0^1 Q^A_i(u)du and compute v^A_i = integral_0^1 (Q^A_i(u)-m^A_i)^2du directly in float64 over the inherited 999-knot linear interior and both constant tails. For every interval with centered endpoints a,b and width h, use h*((a+b)^2+a*a+b*b)/6, exactly the donor helper. Retain the actual jittered GP factor F, original normal block N and all-column row norms d_i = sqrt(sum_j F_ij^2). The active sample becomes S_i = mu_GP_i + sqrt(v^A_i)*z_i with z = (N @ F.T)/d, consumed directly rather than recovered through an inverse CDF of rounded uniforms. Thus GP location/eligibility and adapted native marginal variance remain, while bounded tails, asymmetry and higher moments are replaced jointly by Gaussian shape. Variance zero produces the GP mean exactly; nonfinite/negative variance or malformed dependence inputs are explicit numerical failures handled by the inherited valid bounded fallback. There is no fitted multiplier, variance floor, clipping, GP-amplitude substitution, new model call or extra random draw. Full-coordinate V/C partition, eight views, fitted V preprocessing and nonzero centered query C stay active. This is the registered conditional combination of n-ada68e100737 input adaptation with n-a03f82e62383 shape projection under m-16b934239c55, not a method replacement or technical recovery.

finding_summary.headline: Gaussian shape changed purchases, but full productive gain fell and the transfer prediction failed
finding_summary.insights:
The operation transferred technically, but its predicted joint benefit did not: a modest late gain cannot compensate for lost full-run gain, and a higher count of parent-beating offspring does not ensure more gain mass or a better best molecule. This rules out simple transfer of the earlier shape benefit to the adapted-input host under these conditions. It leaves open the broader use of quantile marginals and their interaction with inputs; neither the earlier results nor the approach receive a new global verdict. The three borrowed elements—quantile moments, integration of the consumed law and separation of latent dependence from marginal choice—all operated. Constant native tails, the campaign’s full-coordinate adapter and the internal Gaussian projection remain deviations from the papers, so their published predictive claims do not explain this outcome.

The search still explores many graphs without reliably reaching broader productive chemistry. Nonempty generic scaffold coverage increased from 1,122 to 1,341, yet several high-score subsets occupied only six to twelve frameworks; the basic-amine high-score subset contracted from fourteen to six. Oversized proposals increased from 112 to 210, and from 32 to 129 late, while very small fragments declined. This is uneven concentration and repeated aromatic assembly, not evidence of universal scaffold collapse. A proposal operator that changes coherent cores and linkers while retaining useful feature connections could address that observed limitation; the experiment does not establish its benefit or identify chemistry as the cause of the score loss. On the actually purchased labels, the unchanged GP/active mean ordering correctly ordered 13,541 of 19,524 strict pairs, versus 13,843 of 19,433 on the Parent’s different trajectory. That descriptive ranking gap cannot attribute an effect to the unchanged mean model. Wider Gaussian 90% intervals covered more purchased labels (84.67% versus 81.70% for the same-state native law), but pinball loss was slightly worse (0.020020 versus 0.019980), so wider coverage is not evidence of useful purchase ranking. Passive alternatives provide no alternative adaptive outcomes, and individual tail, skew and kurtosis contributions remain unresolved.
finding_summary.results:
Gaussian sampling executed correctly in all 435 allocations and preserved the adapted variance, GP means, eligibility and latent draws. It changed 425 allocation sequences and 423 purchase sets, replacing 1,604 purchases relative to the same-state translated-native replay. All 1,548 replacements with a next-fit opportunity entered both real models; 56 terminal replacements were censored. Across all 4,350 purchases, positive gain over actual generating parents fell from 16.68613 to 15.97912, despite more parent-beating purchases (738 versus 697). Late gain over 2,175 purchases rose from 3.91565 to 4.10442. Because both sums had to increase, the registered transfer prediction is refuted. There was no execution failure or missing outcome.

Mean final Top-1 was 0.555785 versus the Parent’s 0.562256, a paired decline of 0.006471. All three seed macros declined, by 0.006454, 0.002774 and 0.010185. Six task/seed endpoints improved and nine fell; the compact fluorinated-ring stream fell in every seed. The formal Anchor mean was 0.607030, leaving a 0.051245 gap and missing the 0.609030 target. The late incumbent gain also fell, from 0.84453 to 0.62099, even as late generating-parent gain increased. These are different quantities, and the incumbent total is already part of endpoint progress.

molecular.headline: Aromatic ring-rich products broaden their frameworks, but oversized assemblies, strained bonds and unspecified stereochemistry persist
molecular.overall_character:
This assessment describes n-741da1149559 against code Parent n-ada68e100737. The frozen comparison independently records child_complete=true and paired_complete=true with Search seeds 0, 1 and 2; all fifteen Child and fifteen published Parent trajectory files were present and read. Each arm supplies 4,350 accepted optimizer proposals, excluding the initial observations, and 2,175 late proposals (optimizer ordinals 146..290 inclusive, evaluations 156..300). These are accepted-stream occurrences across dependent sessions, not all unpurchased generated candidates or independent molecules. No task is missing. The formal Anchor is a different comparison and was not chemically re-audited here.

The Child produces aromatic amides/esters, aza-aromatic ether assemblies, basic amines, carbonyl-rich nitrogen heterocycles and fluorinated fused/bridged rings. RDKit finds rings in 4,342/4,350 products and aromatic atoms in 4,334/4,350, consistent with the digest's near-universal ring and aromatic SMILES counters. Median size is 29 heavy atoms with range 1..119. Ordinary medicinal motifs coexist with highly elaborated graphs; RDKit validity and an observed benchmark score do not demonstrate a synthesis, stability, drug activity or acceptable physical properties. Synthetic plausibility is therefore questionable overall, with credible individual exceptions.

Both size tails remain visible: Child versus Parent counts at <=6 heavy atoms are 9 versus 23, and at >=60 are 210 versus 112; in the late halves these are 4 versus 9 and 129 versus 32. The large tail is concentrated in the repeated aromatic-assembly stream, rather than a universal shift across all objectives. Nonempty typed/generic Murcko scaffold unions are 2,137/1,341 versus 1,813/1,122 for all purchases and 1,040/643 versus 888/521 late. Empty-scaffold occurrences are separately 8 versus 22, and 3 versus 7 late. These are pooled distinct scaffold sets, not sums of session counts; including an empty scaffold as a distinct value would add one and would disagree with this convention. Numerous distinct frameworks coexist with strong motif concentration among high-score subsets; a changed scaffold count is not a chemical explanation of score changes.

Fragment-excluded nearest-initial similarity uses unfolded radius-2 Morgan count fingerprints without chirality and RDKit Tanimoto, taking the maximum over same-session initial molecules with >6 heavy atoms. Query molecules with <=6 atoms are excluded as well. The all-purchase mean is 0.306288 for the Child over 4,341 eligible queries versus 0.316377 over 4,327 for the Parent; late means are 0.250086 over 2,171 versus 0.260794 over 2,166. All sessions have 9 eligible initial references. The 9/23 all-purchase and 4/9 late excluded queries have undefined similarity in this diagnostic, not zero. Lower similarity does not establish useful novelty, and these count-fingerprint numbers should not be pooled with bit-fingerprint or differently filtered historical statistics.

Direct N-halogen/O-halogen bonds occur in 355/142 Child products versus 719/269 Parent products; O-O bonds occur in 48 versus 87. Cyclic allenes, defined as ring carbons doubly bonded to two carbon neighbors, occur in 41 versus 191. Conversely, a broader structural alert for any <=4-membered ring containing a multiple or aromatic bond flags 970 versus 869; this alert includes ordinary small unsaturated rings and is not a verdict of instability. RDKit flags unassigned potential tetrahedral centers in 2,451 versus 1,836 products and assigned centers in none in either arm. All Child products are single connected components without explicit formal charge; this does not imply absence of protonatable amines. The observed reductions in some alerts coexist with more unresolved stereochemistry and a larger upper size tail; no component attribution is made.

Reproducible definitions, all fifteen paired cells, high/low subsets, per-seed best and final records are in policy/scratch/r0065-00-improve-L01/molecular/molecular-audit.json and the fifteen audit-seed-<N>-<task>.json files in the same ticket-specific audit area. Exact input file identities, hashes and missing_paths=[] are in policy/scratch/r0065-00-improve-L01/molecular/source-audit.json. Child staging files were copied byte-for-byte into read-only audit copies inside the run; that manifest records their original absolute trusted citation paths and clearly labels the copies as audit copies, not published node archives. Parent paths remain the published Search trajectories. Full descriptor records are in policy/scratch/r0065-00-improve-L01/molecular/descriptor-rows.json. The frozen request and its hash are retained in the audit; no live scientific snapshot, held-out evidence, Confirmation evidence or oracle was read. Claims below are molecular-score associations only; missing biological motifs cannot be inferred from a task name.

per_task.generated_character: The accepted products have median size 24 heavy atoms, range 9..47, with aromatic amides or esters attached to fused nitrogen/carbon ring systems. The highest-scoring seed representatives are a substituted benzocyclobutene ester (seed 0, evaluation 159, 0.4369542269692598), a compact bridged aza-aromatic pyridyl amide (seed 1, evaluation 293, 0.4562193134122328), and a methoxy/amino-substituted fused aza-aromatic N-methyl anilide (seed 2, evaluation 245, 0.458386638264238). The latter has 23 heavy atoms, four perceived rings and three aromatic rings. These preserve conventional aromatic/carbonyl fragments but combine them with unusual small fused or bridged rings. Synthetic access is less evident than SMILES validity. Neither size tail is populated in either arm. Child nonempty typed/generic scaffold coverage is 313/163 versus Parent 210/99; among the thirty highest observed scores it is 9/7 versus 4/1. Thus the productive subset is less concentrated than the Parent but still a small family of carbonyl-linked aromatic frameworks.
liabilities: The stream contains 311 products with the small-unsaturated-ring alert, plus 20 N-halogen and 10 O-halogen products; these are separate occurrence counts that may overlap.
Duplicated-core growth, strained-looking ring fusion, alkyl halides and late N-chlorination complicate apparent stability and synthetic selectivity.
missing_features: Conventional, stereochemically explicit alternatives around the productive compact aromatic/carbonyl motifs remain incompletely explored: 25 of the thirty highest-score products have unassigned potential centers, with no assigned centers.

Broader productive core/connectivity alternatives remain limited relative to raw scaffold coverage; top thirty products occupy seven generic frameworks. The trajectory does not identify a missing target-specific pharmacophore or establish that another heterocycle would improve the score.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The worst accepted optimizer product, a sulfur-linked, duplicated indole-carboxamide assembly at seed 1 evaluation 32, scores 4.970129253274748e-17. Small disconnected-from-the-core chemical fragments such as fluoromethyl phenyl ether score 4.338023801355052e-10 despite being single connected molecules. Higher scores favor an intermediate-sized retained aromatic/carbonyl assembly: the top thirty contain 22..26 heavy atoms. This is an observed local size-and-arrangement association, not proof of a single required functional group. Paired best scores improve in seed 1 but decrease in seeds 0 and 2. Parent and Child differ in both decorated frameworks and accepted search history, so the broader scaffold set cannot be assigned as the cause. Late final proposals still include N-chlorinated or N-O substituted variants below the best accepted score.

per_task.generated_character: This is the largest and most aromatic stream: median 44 heavy atoms, range 1..119, with 187/870 products at >=60 atoms and 125/435 in the late half. The highest score, 0.6130135051138611 at seed 0 evaluation 284, belongs to a 64-heavy-atom network of phenyl/pyridyl/diazine rings joined through biaryl and aryl-ether connections, including a fused ether-containing closure. RDKit perceives eleven rings, ten aromatic. Seed 1 instead culminates in a substituted dicarbonyl nitrogen heterocycle bearing aza-aryl/ketone groups, and seed 2 in a dicarbonyl fused nitrogen heterocycle with a heteroaryl hydrazide-like linker and N-chlorinated groups. The common fragment vocabulary is plausible; the many connection sites, repeated cores and elaborate closures make the complete assemblies synthetically questionable. Child typed/generic scaffold unions are 599/470 versus 381/289 in the Parent; the top thirty cover 26/22 versus 8/5.
liabilities: Repetition of many aromatic/aza-aromatic units gives substantial size, coupling selectivity and conformational burdens; no synthesis or physical-property measurements support these structures.
Across all accepted proposals, 75 have N-halogen bonds and 10 O-halogen bonds; the seed-0 top aromatic assembly lacks these alerts, demonstrating that the stream is chemically heterogeneous.
missing_features: Compact alternatives that retain productive heteroaromatic connectivity are underrepresented at the Child high-score end: the Parent supplies stronger compact examples, while the Child repeatedly extends ring networks.

Chemically conventional terminal heteroatom substituents are not consistently retained in the other seed families; high seed-2 candidates still use N-halogen bonds. The scores do not establish a particular missing hydrogen-bond pattern or desired biological scaffold.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The smallest accepted product, F, scores 0.5, while halogenated phenol scores 0.5052914719111032 and a peroxide-linked aza-aromatic fragment 0.5100965759438103. The high-score seed-0 family repeatedly accumulates aza-aromatic ring and ether motifs. Its top-thirty pooled products average 76.2 heavy atoms, with 21 at >=60 atoms. This supports an association between repeated aromatic motifs and the local high scores; it does not establish that growth itself is useful. The Parent's top thirty have 43..55 atoms and its best seed-2 score is 0.6324541616056452, above the Child's best, while Child seeds 0 and 1 improve their paired endpoints. Compact alternatives can therefore be competitive in the supplied evidence, and no universal minimum size is justified. The three seeds occupy substantially different chemotypes; the digest's final records are only the end of seed 2.

per_task.generated_character: Aromatic/basic-amine chemistry dominates the high-score end. The best molecule (seed 1, evaluation 292, 0.9999993589104218) is a 26-heavy-atom flexible tertiary aliphatic amine connecting a phenolic/methyl aryl arm to a dichloro/aniline aryl arm; it has two aromatic rings and one unassigned potential center. The other seed leaders instead use substantially bridged polycyclic amines, with six or seven perceived rings and multiple unassigned centers. The whole stream has median 32 heavy atoms, range 13..102; seventeen proposals reach >=60 atoms but none do so late. Conventional amine/aryl combinations are credible medicinal chemistry motifs; the highly bridged alternatives require more caution. Child typed/generic scaffolds are 477/321 versus Parent 506/381; top-thirty coverage contracts to 6/6 versus 14/14.
liabilities: The whole stream includes 116 O-halogen, 24 N-halogen and 14 cyclic-allene products, even though the high thirty have none of these direct halogen alerts.
Flexible arylalkyl amines, extensive halogen substitution and densely bridged alternatives raise distinct selectivity, conformational and synthetic questions that the recorded scores do not resolve.
missing_features: Stereochemical definition is absent despite unassigned potential centers in 863/870 proposals and all thirty highest-score products; the scores shown do not establish which stereoisomer, if any, would be preferred.

Productive scaffold alternatives around the successful basic-amine/aromatic arrangement remain concentrated in six generic frameworks in the high thirty. Basic amine centers themselves are present; the missing evidence concerns tractable, well-defined alternatives rather than absence of nitrogen functionality.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The high thirty have 23..27 heavy atoms, two aromatic rings each and available aliphatic amine centers. At the low end, the N-chloro amide/sulfonyl-pyrrolidine derivative scores 0.00016650955053713697, and a small dichloroaryl sulfonate scores 0.00024675866379847753. Thus, in these examples, a well-separated aromatic/basic-amine arrangement outperforms the sulfonyl/carbonyl-heavy or reduced fragments. Neither aromaticity nor chlorination alone is sufficient. The near-unit recorded scores are benchmark observations, not independent binding or pharmacology evidence. Seed 1 improves over its Parent while seeds 0 and 2 decrease; more elaborate rings are not consistently rewarded, because the best Child representative is comparatively simple.

per_task.generated_character: Products combine alkyl/ethoxy-substituted aromatic rings with carbonyl-rich nitrogen rings, tertiary amines, fused rings and larger cyclic connections. Median size is 32 heavy atoms, range 1..69. The best molecule at seed 0 evaluation 254 scores 0.23847116219506703: a 34-heavy-atom structure containing two aryl groups, a dicarbonyl nitrogen ring and a tertiary amine-bearing cyclic connection. The other seed leaders retain related dicarbonyl/amine/aryl chemistry. The high thirty have 30..36 heavy atoms and mostly four-ring frameworks. Synthetic plausibility is mixed: functional groups are conventional, but large-ring closures, unsaturation placement and stereochemical selectivity are not specified. Child typed/generic scaffold unions are 436/272 versus Parent 409/244; top-thirty coverage is 15/12 versus 20/13.
liabilities: Tiny fragments discard the observed useful combination of features, while a separate large-size tail adds complexity without a consistent score benefit.
Small unsaturated-ring alerts occur in 147 proposals and direct N-halogen bonds in 18; elaborate cyclic amide/amine connectivity is not a demonstrated synthetic route.
missing_features: Coherent alternatives to the recurring aryl/dicarbonyl/amine connectivity are not well established at the high-score end; twelve generic high-thirty frameworks provide less coverage than the full 272-framework pool.

Explicit stereochemical alternatives are missing: 27 of the high thirty have unassigned potential centers. The evidence does not demonstrate a benefit from assigning them, or identify an exact missing target motif.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Single-carbon products and OO score zero; COCCl scores 0.014555562743489544. Higher scores retain the multi-part aromatic/dicarbonyl/amine assembly, but neither size nor the presence of a carbonyl alone explains the ordering: the low thirty include both tiny fragments and large molecules. Across the full stream there are eight <=6-heavy-atom and six >=60-heavy-atom products, including three and four respectively late. Child high-score products have fewer aromatic rings on average than the Parent high-score set, while endpoints are slightly higher in seeds 0 and 1 and slightly lower in seed 2. The observed gradient supports preserving connected arrangements of several features rather than simply adding aromatic rings. The low absolute endpoint cannot reveal an unseen reference structure or a uniquely missing fragment.

per_task.generated_character: This stream stays within 9..48 heavy atoms with median 27 and no products in either monitored size tail. It favors fluorinated nitrogen/carbonyl heterocycles with unsaturated or small alicyclic appendages, aza-aromatic/phenolic groups and many fused/bridged connections. The best Child (seed 1 evaluation 270, 0.5103407336474033) has 25 heavy atoms, five perceived rings, two aromatic rings, an imino group, a carbonyl, a fluorinated hydroxy-diene ring and a small bridged unsaturated connection; four potential centers are unassigned. Seed 0 favors a difluorocyclopropyl-containing fused heterocycle and seed 2 a fluorinated cyclobutene-containing dicarbonyl heterocycle with an N-F bond. These are chemically specific, compact structures, but substantial strain and unusual heteroatom bonds make their synthetic plausibility questionable. Typed/generic scaffold unions are 347/155 versus Parent 343/156, and top-thirty coverage is 13/7 versus 15/9.
liabilities: The complete stream contains 218 N-halogen products, 27 cyclic allenes and 279 small-unsaturated-ring alerts; these overlapping descriptors are chemical caution signals, not measured instability.

The best structures include densely fused or bridged unsaturation, small fluorinated rings and multiple unassigned centers; neutral SMILES does not establish the preferred protonation or tautomeric form.
missing_features: Stable-looking conventional bond environments around the compact productive heterocycles remain inconsistent: fourteen of the high thirty contain direct N-halogen bonds and twenty carry the small-unsaturated-ring alert.

Stereochemical resolution is absent in all thirty high-score products. The observed scores support neither a preferred stereoisomer nor an assumption that supplying a named reference-drug motif would be legal or useful.
Alternatives that preserve the useful compact polar/fluorinated arrangement while changing strained connections remain insufficiently represented to establish a reliable local chemical gradient.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The poorest accepted optimizer example, a larger hydroxylamine/hemiaminal-bearing cyclic amine joined to a dicarbonyl heterocycle, scores 1.6160016138490882e-18. Another low example retains the dicarbonyl heterocycle and phenol but lacks the successful compact fluorinated appendage pattern, scoring 1.9215685034033696e-09. The higher-scoring set is compact and combines fluorination with nitrogen/carbonyl and ring features; fluorination or ring count alone does not explain the full gradient. All three Child best scores are below their paired Parent values (0.49317199895702235, 0.6054215806683655 and 0.5147249403189217 respectively). Similar size and scaffold counts therefore do not imply preserved productive chemical arrangements. The remaining desired target-specific chemistry cannot be inferred from these trajectories.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-741da1149559 against published Parent n-ada68e100737, same Search seeds 0/1/2 and accepted-stream definitions. Direct N-halogen/O-halogen molecule counts decrease to 355/142 from 719/269, and cyclic allenes to 41 from 191, yet 970 products carry a broader small-unsaturated-ring alert versus 869. Some high-score products still contain N-halogen bonds, whereas other successful amine/aromatic and carbonyl/aromatic products do not. These are conditional structural associations, not component attribution, reaction outcomes or universal invalidity rules.
transferable_gaps.gap: Conventional bond environments are still not reliably retained around productive molecular cores.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide chemically coherent local bond and ring alternatives around productive cores, with explicit awareness of heteroatom-halogen bonds and small-ring unsaturation. Keep real session score feedback authoritative; any changed proposal chemistry requires its own task-agnostic test rather than an assumed beneficial filter.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-741da1149559, matched Search panel against n-ada68e100737: <=6-heavy-atom counts are 9 versus 23 and >=60 counts 210 versus 112 over 4,350 purchases per arm; late counts are 4 versus 9 and 129 versus 32 over 2,175. Actual tiny fragments reach zero or the observed floor. Large repeated aza-aromatic assemblies occupy one high-score subset, but the paired Parent also supplies competitive smaller assemblies. Counts and conditions are specific to these accepted adaptive histories.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator still loses useful feature connectivity at the small end and repeatedly overassembles aromatic motifs at the large end.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make assembly-preserving edits and compact core/linker alternatives available without destroying combinations of features that the current session rewards. Track both tails separately and let local observations determine useful molecular extent; neither unrestricted growth nor universal shrinkage is supported.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-741da1149559 under the same complete Search panel: nonempty typed/generic Murcko unions increase to 2,137/1,341 from Parent 1,813/1,122, while high-thirty subsets still occupy only 6, 7 or 12 generic frameworks in several streams. One carbonyl/aromatic stream expands its high-thirty coverage from one to seven generic frameworks, but another basic-amine stream contracts from fourteen to six. Fragment-excluded nearest-initial count similarity also shifts, with no demonstrated mediation of scores. Empty scaffolds and fingerprint conventions retain their audit definitions.
transferable_gaps.gap: Broad graph exploration does not consistently supply broad productive core chemistry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Distinguish genuine core/linker changes from peripheral decoration and maintain chemically interpretable alternatives around useful functional-group combinations. Measure productive scaffold coverage separately from unique SMILES, raw scaffold count or distance from initial molecules; no particular generator component is identified as the cause here.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-741da1149559 versus n-ada68e100737, complete accepted Search panel: RDKit identifies unassigned potential centers in 2,451 versus 1,836 products and assigned centers in none. Every high-thirty product in two distinct compact amine/fluorinated-ring streams has an unassigned center. The digest reports zero stereocentre annotations throughout. These are representation findings, not evidence of experimentally isolable stereoisomers or score sensitivity.
transferable_gaps.gap: Three-dimensional products remain stereochemically unspecified even when they dominate the high-score subsets.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support consistent stereochemical representations and, where the scoring interface can distinguish them, alternative stereochemical assignments around promising substituted rings, bridges and side chains. First establish sensitivity within the existing contract; the observed omission does not by itself justify spending budget on indiscriminate stereoisomer enumeration.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
